examples.ko: 학교 앞에 졸업을 축하하는 현수막이 내걸렸어요.
examples.en: A banner congratulating the graduates was hung in front of the school.
On holidays, a Taegukgi flag is hung outside every shop.
Election posters are hung along the street.

examples.ko: 문 앞에 '휴업'이라는 팻말이 내걸린 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a sign saying 'Closed' hung on the door.

examples.ko: 건물 벽에 큰 광고판이 내걸리면서 동네가 밝아졌어요.
examples.en: A big billboard went up on the building wall and the neighborhood got brighter.

examples.ko: 다음 주부터 극장에 새 영화 간판이 내걸릴 거예요.
examples.en: From next week, the sign for the new movie will go up at the theater.

explain: '걸리다'와 달리 현수막, 간판, 깃발처럼 사람들이 볼 수 있게 바깥이나 앞쪽에 높이 달린다는 느낌이에요. 짝이 되는 능동형은 '내걸다'예요. '조건이 내걸리다', '공약을 내걸다'처럼 뜻을 내세운다는 표현으로도 써요.

phrases.en: The sign was finally hung at the new shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간판이나 현수막이 사람들이 볼 수 있는 곳에 달릴 때 써요. 이미 달린 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a sign or banner is put up where people can see it. It describes the result.

phrases.en: Festival flags are hung along the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걸린 상태가 계속되는 모습을 말하는 활용이에요. 풍경을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form that shows the state of being hung continues. It is often used to describe scenery.

phrases.en: The mayoral candidate put forward a new pledge.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내걸리다'의 능동형이에요. 물건을 달 때도 쓰고, 공약처럼 뜻을 내세울 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form of '내걸리다'. It is used for hanging things and for putting forward a pledge.
phrases.en_equiv: to hang out; to put forward

explain_en: Unlike plain '걸리다', it suggests something is put up outside or at the front where people can see it, like a banner, sign or flag. The active counterpart is '내걸다'. It is also used for putting forward things like conditions or pledges, as in '공약을 내걸다'.

examples.en: Our team's fierce comeback began in the second half.
The gap in approval ratings narrowed because of the second-place candidate's fierce chase.

examples.ko: 마지막 구간에서 맹추격을 펼쳤지만 아쉽게 졌어요.
examples.en: We made a fierce push in the last stretch but sadly lost.
Thanks to the fierce comeback, the game was exciting until the end.

examples.ko: 선두를 향한 맹추격은 결국 실패로 끝났어요.
examples.en: The fierce chase of the leader ended in failure.

examples.ko: 맹추격으로 점수 차이를 한 골로 줄였어요.
examples.en: With a fierce push, they cut the score gap to one goal.

explain: 스포츠, 선거, 경제 뉴스에서 뒤에 있던 쪽이 앞선 쪽을 빠르게 따라잡을 때 많이 써요. '맹추격을 하다/펼치다/벌이다', '맹추격에 나서다'처럼 말해요. '맹훈련', '맹활약'처럼 '맹-'이 붙으면 기세가 거세다는 느낌이 더해져요.

phrases.en: Our team mounted a fierce chase in the second half.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에서 열심히 따라잡는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes catching up hard from behind.

phrases.en: The second-place team set out on a fierce chase to catch the leader.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따라잡으려고 행동을 시작한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means starting to take action to catch up.
phrases.en_equiv: to set out on a fierce chase

phrases.example: 선두 팀이 2위 팀의 맹추격을 받고 있어요.
phrases.en: The leading team is under fierce pursuit from the second-place team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쫓기는 앞선 쪽의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the leading side that is being chased.

explain_en: It is common in sports, election and business news when the side that was behind catches up fast. You say '맹추격을 하다/펼치다/벌이다' or '맹추격에 나서다'. Like '맹훈련' and '맹활약', the '맹-' prefix adds a fierce, forceful feel.

en: to emit; to discharge; (a player) to release from a team

examples.en: The factory emits smoke into the sky.

examples.ko: 난로는 열을 방출해서 방을 따뜻하게 해요.
examples.en: The heater gives off heat and warms the room.
The club released the underperforming player.

examples.ko: 식물은 햇빛을 받으면 산소를 방출하는 일을 해요.
examples.en: Plants release oxygen when they receive sunlight.
If you release dangerous substances, you are punished.

examples.ko: 몸은 땀으로 열을 방출할 수 있어요.
examples.en: The body can release heat through sweat.

explain: 방출하다는 열·빛·가스·에너지를 밖으로 내보낼 때 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 쓰레기나 오염 물질은 '배출하다'가 더 자주 쓰여요. 팀이 선수를 내보낸다는 뜻으로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The factory sends smoke outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy word used in everyday speech.

phrases.example: 이 차는 나쁜 가스를 방출하지 않아요.
phrases.en: This car does not emit harmful gas.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내보내지 않는다는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form: does not emit.

phrases.en: The team released a struggling player.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팀이 선수를 내보낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a team lets a player go.

explain_en: Active, gives off heat, energy or gas; also cuts a player. 방출하다 is a formal word for sending out heat, light, gas or energy. For waste and pollutants, '배출하다' is more common. It is also widely used for a team letting a player go.

t90.ax: The factory emits smoke into the sky.

examples.ko: 요행히 비가 오기 전에 집에 도착했어요.
examples.en: Luckily, I got home before the rain started.
Fortunately, nobody was hurt.

examples.ko: 요행히 마지막 버스를 탈 수 있었어요.
examples.en: By luck I was able to catch the last bus.

examples.ko: 길을 잃었지만 요행히 친절한 분을 만났어요.
examples.en: I got lost, but luckily I met a kind person.

examples.ko: 요행히 시험 문제가 제가 공부한 데서 나왔어요.
examples.en: Luckily, the exam questions came from what I had studied.

examples.ko: 요행히 표가 한 장 남아 있었어요.
examples.en: By good luck, one ticket was left.

explain: '다행히'와 비슷하지만 운 좋게 위기를 넘기거나 뜻밖에 잘된 상황에 더 어울리고, 다소 글말 같은 느낌이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '다행히'를 훨씬 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Fortunately, the road wasn't congested.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '요행히'보다 훨씬 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used far more than 'yohaenghi' in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: I luckily caught the last bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요행히'보다 쉽고 말하기 편한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more casual expression than 'yohaenghi'.

phrases.example: 요행히도 시험 문제가 내가 공부한 부분에서 나왔어요.
phrases.en: Luckily, the exam questions came from the part I studied.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도'를 붙여 뜻밖의 행운을 더 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'do' emphasizes the unexpected good fortune.

explain_en: Written; unexpected stroke of luck, not relief. It is close to '다행히', but fits better when you escape trouble or things turn out well by chance, and it sounds somewhat written. In everyday speech '다행히' is much more common.

en: to pull up; to refloat; to salvage

examples.en: They raised the car that had fallen into the sea.
They plan to raise the ship with a crane.

examples.ko: 침몰한 배를 인양하는 데 한 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Raising the sunken ship took a month.
Before raising the relics, they check their condition.
They decided to raise the ship and investigate the cause.
Relics that were raised are kept in a museum.

explain: '끌어올리다'는 위로 올리는 일 전체에 쓰고, '인양하다'는 물속에 가라앉은 큰 물건을 끌어올릴 때만 써요. 목적어는 '배', '차', '유물' 같은 것이에요. 일이 이루어진 쪽에서는 '인양되다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The sunken ship was raised yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끌어올려지는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요. 주어는 배나 차예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the thing raised; the subject is a ship or car.

phrases.en: We plan to raise the relics next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 할 일을 말할 때 '-ㄹ 계획'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -ㄹ 계획 to talk about a future plan.

phrases.en: The crane pulled up the car from the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인양하다'보다 쉽고, 위로 올리는 일 전체에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 인양하다 and works for any lifting upward.

explain_en: '끌어올리다' covers pulling anything upward, but '인양하다' is used only for raising large things that sank in water. The object is something like a ship, a car or relics. When the thing is the subject, it becomes '인양되다'.

t90.ax: Raising the sunken ship took a month.

examples.en: Let's wrap up here for now and take a break.

examples.ko: 보고서 작성은 일단락 지었으니 이제 발표를 준비해요.
examples.en: I've finished the report for now, so I'm preparing the presentation.

examples.ko: 이 일이 일단락이 되면 같이 여행 가요.
examples.en: When this work is wrapped up, let's go on a trip together.

examples.ko: 오늘 일은 여기서 일단락으로 하고 퇴근해요.
examples.en: Let's call today's work done here and go home.
I accepted the apology and put the matter to rest.

examples.ko: 공사가 일단락은 됐지만 마무리 청소가 남았어요.
examples.en: The construction is done for now, but the final cleaning remains.

explain: 대부분 '일단락 짓다', '일단락이 되다'처럼 써요. 완전히 끝났다기보다 한 고비를 넘겼다는 느낌이라 뒤에 '아직 할 일이 남았다'가 이어질 수 있어요. 일상에서는 '일단 마무리하다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 부분은 일단락 짓고 다음으로 넘어가요.
phrases.en: Let's wrap up this part and move on to the next.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 일을 한 단계 정리할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for a person wrapping up a stage of work.

phrases.example: 회의가 일단락이 되면 같이 점심 먹어요.
phrases.en: Once the meeting wraps up, let's have lunch together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 한 단계 정리되었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a matter has reached a stopping point.

phrases.en: Let's wrap up today's work for now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '일단락'보다 이렇게 쉽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech, people say it this easy way instead of 일단락.

explain_en: It is mostly used as '일단락 짓다' or '일단락이 되다'. It feels less like totally finished and more like getting past one stage, so 'but there is still work left' can follow. In daily talk people also say '일단 마무리하다'.

examples.en: Everyone hopes for an end to the war.
Experts say the end of the disease is near.
When the declaration of the end came out, people were happy.

examples.ko: 이번 협정은 오랜 갈등의 종식이 될 거예요.
examples.en: This agreement will mark the end of a long conflict.
We gathered for the end of violence.
We still need time before it is over.

explain: 종식은 오래 이어진 나쁜 일이나 큰 문제가 완전히 끝난다는 뜻으로 써요. '끝'이나 '마지막'과 달리, 전쟁·병·갈등처럼 심각한 일에만 주로 써요. '종식을 선언하다', '종식되다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The government declared the end of the epidemic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 문제가 끝났다고 공식적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when officially declaring a big problem is over.

phrases.en: I hope the war comes to an end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '종식'을 동사로 바꿔서 스스로 끝나는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, describing something coming to an end.

phrases.en: We work for an early end to the infectious disease.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조기'는 '빠른'이라는 뜻으로, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: 조기 means 'early', and the phrase is common in the news.

explain_en: Formal; complete end of war, conflict or an epidemic. 종식 is for a serious, long-running problem finally coming to an end, such as a war, disease or conflict. Unlike plain 끝 (end), it is not used for everyday things like a class or a movie. Common forms are 종식을 선언하다 and 종식되다.

dis.h: Complete end of something bad, like war

p.n: 종료 only states that it ended; 종식 says the bad thing is gone for good.

t90.ax: We gathered for the end of violence.

examples.en: He is known as a heavyweight in the political world.

examples.ko: 업계 거물이 우리 회사에 투자하기로 했어요.
examples.en: A big name in the industry decided to invest in our company.

examples.ko: 이번 모임에는 재계 거물들이 많이 와요.
examples.en: Many business tycoons are coming to this gathering.

examples.ko: 그는 거물에게도 할 말은 하는 사람이에요.
examples.en: He is someone who speaks his mind even to big shots.

examples.ko: 저는 거물급 인사를 만날 기회가 거의 없어요.
examples.en: I hardly ever get a chance to meet top-level figures.

examples.ko: 작은 가게로 시작해서 지금은 거물이 됐어요.
examples.en: He started with a small shop and has now become a magnate.

explain: 정치, 재계, 연예계처럼 한 분야에서 영향력이 큰 사람을 말해요. '거물급'이나 '거물 정치인'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 자주 써요. 돈을 많이 쓰는 손님은 '큰손'이라고도 하지만, '거물'은 영향력이 큰 사람에게 써요.

phrases.en: A very important figure attended the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거물'에 '-급'을 붙여 그만한 수준의 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds '-급' to mean someone of that big-shot level.

phrases.en: He is a well-known heavyweight politician in the region.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거물' 뒤에 직업을 붙여 분야를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a job after '거물' to show the field.

phrases.en: He is a big name in the film industry.
phrases.nuance_ko: '업계의' 뒤에 써서 한 분야에서 영향력이 큰 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used after '업계의' for a very influential person in a field.

explain_en: Big shot with great influence in an industry or field. It refers to someone with great influence in a field such as politics, business, or entertainment. It is often extended as '거물급' or '거물 정치인'. A big spender may be called '큰손', but '거물' is for people with great influence.

en: displaced person (from one's hometown); refugee who cannot return home

examples.ko: 할아버지는 전쟁 때 고향을 떠난 실향민이에요.
examples.en: My grandfather is a displaced person who left his hometown during the war.

examples.ko: 명절이 되면 실향민들은 고향 생각이 더 간절해져요.
examples.en: On holidays, displaced people long for their hometowns even more.
Many displaced people live in this village.

examples.ko: 실향민 가족이 이산가족 상봉 소식을 기다리고 있어요.
examples.en: A displaced family is waiting for news of a family reunion.
I heard the stories of elderly displaced people on the news.

examples.ko: 실향민에게 고향은 가고 싶어도 갈 수 없는 곳이에요.
examples.en: For a displaced person, hometown is a place they cannot go back to even if they want to.

explain: 한국에서는 주로 전쟁과 분단 때문에 북쪽에 있는 고향을 떠나온 사람을 가리킬 때가 많아요. 재해로 집을 잃은 사람은 '이재민', 나라 밖으로 피한 사람은 '난민'이라고 해서 서로 달라요.

phrases.en: Our neighbors are a family of displaced people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고향을 떠나온 사람이 있는 가족을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a family that includes someone who left their hometown.

phrases.example: 영화는 실향민의 아픔을 잘 보여 줬어요.
phrases.en: The movie showed well the pain of displaced people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'를 붙여 이들이 느끼는 마음을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 의, it's often used to talk about what these people feel.

phrases.en: On holidays, many displaced people visit Imjingak.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들'을 붙여 여러 사람을 한꺼번에 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 들, it refers to many such people at once.

explain_en: In Korea it is often used for people who left their hometowns in the North because of the war and division. It differs from '이재민' (people who lost their homes in a disaster) and '난민' (refugees who fled abroad).

examples.ko: 이 길은 사고가 많아서 악명이 높아요.
examples.en: This road has a bad reputation because of many accidents.

examples.ko: 악명 높은 교통 체증에 한 시간 갇혀 있었어요.
examples.en: I was stuck for an hour in the notorious traffic jam.
That restaurant became notorious for its unfriendliness.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 야근이 많다는 악명 때문에 지원자가 줄었어요.
examples.en: Because of the company's reputation for long overtime, applicants decreased.
Despite his bad reputation, he was actually a kind person.
It was a notoriously dangerous mountain road, so I drove carefully.

explain: 나쁜 일로 유명하다는 말이에요. '악명이 높다', '악명이 자자하다'처럼 써요. '유명하다'는 좋은 뜻과 나쁜 뜻 모두 가능하지만 악명은 반드시 나쁜 쪽이에요. 좋은 일로 유명한 것은 '명성'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: That restaurant is notorious for being unfriendly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 소문이 널리 퍼졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the bad reputation has spread widely.

phrases.en: The notorious thief was caught.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~ㄴ' 형태로 명사 앞에 붙여서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun.

phrases.example: 그 팀은 거친 경기로 악명을 떨쳤어요.
phrases.en: That team became notorious for rough play.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일로 이름이 널리 알려졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a name becomes widely known for bad things.

explain_en: Bad reputation or notoriety, for people or places (악명이 높다) It means being famous for something bad. It is used as '악명이 높다' or '악명이 자자하다'. '유명하다' can be good or bad, but 악명 is always negative. Being famous for good things is called '명성'.

examples.en: A story about the two actors' romance appeared in the news.

examples.ko: 그 정치인은 젊은 시절 염문을 뿌렸다고 해요.
examples.en: They say that politician was rumored to have many romances in his youth.
The singer caught up in a romance rumor held a press conference.
The two strongly denied the rumors of a romance.
The romance rumor spread quickly.

examples.ko: 그 영화감독은 염문 때문에 한동안 일을 못 했어요.
examples.en: That film director couldn't work for a while because of a romance scandal.

explain: 외래어 '스캔들'과 달리 연애나 사랑에 관한 소문에만 써요. 주로 연예인이나 유명인 기사에서 보는 글말이고, 일상 대화에서는 '연애설'이라고 많이 해요.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 젊을 때 여러 사람과 염문을 뿌렸어요.
phrases.en: That actor was linked romantically with many people when he was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번이 아니라 여러 사람과 연애 소문이 난다는 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스나 이야기에서 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It suggests romance rumors with several people, not just once. It is used in news and storytelling.
phrases.en_equiv: be rumored to have many romances

explain_en: Rumor of a love affair, usually about celebrities; news style. Unlike the loanword '스캔들', it is used only for rumors about romance. It is mostly written language seen in articles about celebrities, and in conversation people often say '연애설'.

en: influential person; big gun; local notable

examples.en: An influential person in that area sponsored the event.
I started the business without help from anyone powerful.
The influential people of the village gathered and held a meeting.
There is a rumor that he is close to a powerful figure in politics.
If I ask a powerful person, will things work out quickly?

examples.ko: 유력자라고 해서 법을 어겨도 되는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being influential doesn't mean you can break the law.

explain: 정치, 경제, 지역 사회에서 영향력이 큰 사람을 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '실력자'가 있고, 연줄이나 힘을 가진 사람이라는 느낌이 있어서 문맥에 따라 약간 부정적으로 들리기도 해요.

phrases.en: Influential local figures attended the gathering.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 동네나 지방에서 힘이 큰 사람을 말할 때 앞에 '지역'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: '지역' is put before it for a person with power in a town or region.

phrases.en: The power broker of that company made the decision.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 '실력자'는 실제로 일을 움직이는 힘이 있는 사람이라는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, but '실력자' suggests someone who actually moves things.

phrases.en: He met an influential person and asked for help.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘 있는 사람에게 부탁하러 가는 장면에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in scenes of going to ask a powerful person for help.

explain_en: Influential person of standing in a community — social weight, often local. It refers to a person with great influence in politics, business or a local community. A similar word is '실력자', and it suggests someone with connections and power, so depending on context it can sound slightly negative.

t90.ax: Being influential doesn't mean you can break the law.

examples.en: The police finally caught the real culprit.
Evidence came out that the real culprit is someone else.
In the final episode, the real culprit was an unexpected person.

examples.ko: 처음에 잡힌 사람은 진범과 아무 관계가 없었어요.
examples.en: The person first caught had nothing to do with the real culprit.

examples.ko: 모두가 그를 진범으로 믿었지만 사실은 아니었어요.
examples.en: Everyone believed he was the real culprit, but he wasn't.

examples.ko: 누가 진범인지 끝까지 알 수 없었어요.
examples.en: We couldn't tell who the real culprit was until the end.

explain: 다른 사람이 억울하게 의심받을 때 '진짜 범인'을 가리키는 말이에요. '진범을 잡다/밝히다', '진범이 따로 있다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: The police finally caught the real culprit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation.

phrases.en: The real culprit in this case is someone else.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의심받은 사람이 범인이 아닐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the suspect is innocent.
phrases.en_equiv: the real culprit is someone else

phrases.en: The real criminal hasn't been caught yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '진짜 범인'이 더 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier everyday wording.

explain_en: It points to the true criminal, especially when someone else has been wrongly suspected. It is often used as '진범을 잡다/밝히다' and '진범이 따로 있다'.

examples.en: He was a revolutionary who tried to change the country.

examples.ko: 그 혁명가는 평생 자유를 위해 싸웠어요.
examples.en: That revolutionary fought for freedom all his life.
The revolutionaries gathered in secret and made a plan.
I watched a movie about the life of a revolutionary.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 꿈은 혁명가가 되는 거였어요.
examples.en: My childhood dream was to become a revolutionary.
For the young revolutionary, time was always short.

explain: 사회나 정치 체제를 크게 뒤집으려고 앞장서는 사람을 가리켜요. '운동가'는 사회운동을 하는 사람을 넓게 가리키는 말이라, 혁명가는 그보다 체제를 바꾸려는 뜻이 훨씬 강해요. 역사 이야기나 영화, 책에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 이 영화는 한 혁명가의 삶을 그렸어요.
phrases.en: This movie portrays the life of a revolutionary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책이나 영화에서 인물의 이야기를 소개할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to introduce a person's story in books or films.

phrases.en: Young revolutionaries gathered in the square.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이나 특징을 앞에 붙여 사람을 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put an age or trait before it to describe the person.

phrases.example: 그는 가난한 집에서 자라 혁명가가 되었어요.
phrases.en: He grew up in a poor family and became a revolutionary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 사람이 변해 가는 과정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when describing how a person turns into something.

explain_en: It refers to a person who takes the lead in overturning a social or political system. '운동가' (activist) covers anyone in social movements, so 혁명가 carries a much stronger sense of changing the system itself. It often appears in history, films and books.

examples.en: Dairy farming is well developed in this region.
My uncle is in dairy farming and raises cows.

examples.ko: 낙농업에 종사하는 사람들이 우유 값을 걱정해요.
examples.en: People working in dairy farming are worried about milk prices.

examples.ko: 낙농업은 아침 일찍 시작하는 힘든 일이에요.
examples.en: Dairy farming is hard work that starts early in the morning.
He studied dairy farming at university and opened a ranch.

examples.ko: 여름에 너무 더우면 낙농업에도 피해가 커요.
examples.en: When summer is too hot, dairy farming also suffers a lot of damage.

explain: 소를 키워 우유를 얻는 산업이에요. 그 일을 하는 농가는 '낙농가'라고 하고, 고기를 얻으려고 가축을 키우는 일까지 합친 큰 말은 '축산업'이에요.

phrases.en: The dairy farmer milks the cows from dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낙농업을 하는 집이나 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the household or person that does dairy farming.

phrases.en: My family does dairy farming in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 일을 직업으로 한다는 뜻의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing meaning to do this work as a living.

phrases.en: Cheese and butter are typical dairy products.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우유로 만든 식품을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for foods made from milk.

explain_en: It is the industry of raising cows to get milk. A farm or farmer doing this is a '낙농가', and the wider term that also covers raising animals for meat is '축산업'.
